tone.name: Adventure
tone.description: Movement and discovery. Maps, journeys, ticking clocks, and brave choices. Short, active sentences.

settings.name: School on a moon base during the eclipse week

goals.name: Stop a sabotage before a deadline
goals.description: Someone plans to ruin an event or a machine. Find the plan before it happens.

goals.name: Identify a secret admirer
goals.description: Anonymous gifts and notes arrive. Find out who sends them.

twists.name: The heir in plain sight
twists.description: The missing heir works in the house as a member of staff.

twists.name: The animal did it
twists.description: An animal caused the mess or the loss. For kids, it is a harmless and funny version.

twists.name: The victim set the trail
twists.description: The victim left the puzzle trail on purpose, before it happened.

frames.name: The ghost hunter show
frames.description: You review the material of a ghost hunting TV show.

frames.name: The secret society initiation
frames.description: A secret society invites you, and the puzzles are your initiation.

motifs.name: Clocks
motifs.puzzle_skins: Clock hands as codes, stopped times as alibis, chimes as counts, and a timetable as the final lock.

motifs.name: Lighthouses
motifs.puzzle_skins: Light patterns as Morse, a keeper's log as a timeline, and tide tables as calendar math.

plots: A stormy night in a gothic mansion, with a butler.
A rich old man poisoned at the reading of his will.
Poison in the wine glass at a dinner party.
The culprit is an evil twin that nobody mentioned.
The culprit has amnesia and did it without knowing.
The detective's long-lost relative is the culprit.
The famous riddle with a changed answer.
A secret passage that the floor plan never shows.

audience_rule.notes: Ages 10 to 13 with adults. Theft, sabotage, a kidnapping with a safe return, or a faked death. Easy to medium puzzles. 11 to 12 pt type and a moderate amount of text.

mechanics.name: Word Search With Leftover Message
mechanics.summary: Find the theme words, then the unused letters spell a message.

mechanics.name: Maze With Letters on the Path
mechanics.summary: Solve a maze, and the letters on the true path spell the answer.

mechanics.name: Pigpen Cipher
mechanics.summary: Letters become pieces of tic-tac-toe and X grids, with or without dots.

mechanics.name: Clock Hands Code
mechanics.summary: Clock times encode digits, letters, or numbers to add.

mechanics.name: Whodunit Deduction
mechanics.summary: Players use all the evidence to name the culprit, the method, and the motive.

mechanics.name: Arithmetic Lock
mechanics.summary: Numbers found in several documents combine by a stated formula into the lock code.

mechanics.name: Shredded Document Strips
mechanics.summary: A document cut into vertical strips goes back into order.

mechanics.name: Nonogram
mechanics.summary: Number clues for each row and column reveal a picture of a digit, letter, or object.

mechanics.name: Anagram
mechanics.summary: The letters of a phrase rearrange into the answer.

mechanics.name: Book Cipher Over Kit Documents
mechanics.summary: Number triples point to a document, a line, and a word in the kit.

mechanics.name: Map Grid Coordinates
mechanics.summary: Coordinates such as C4 point to map places, and their initials spell the answer.

mechanics.name: Visual Morse Code
mechanics.summary: Short and long marks hidden in a picture or a log spell letters in Morse code.
